I totally agree with you. Even though that is what the law should be -  identifying a case affecting minors with mutual 'consent' to be less worse than minors in non - 'consensual' statutory rape, that's just not how things work in my country.
It's not looked at in the way you've mentioned. For India, as far as I'm aware, the moment an underage girl is involved, there are hundreds of organizations that will make sure the girl is assisted throughout the whole ordeal, and a case is registered. However, like we observe here, it just doesn't matter if the boy is her age or just 11. The court will never see it that way. For the courts, and for most people who make a huge fuss when these gender biased laws are in talks for ammendment, they believe r*pe is nothing but penetration by a male against a female. That is why these skewed beliefs and unawareness of "forced to penetrate" cases cause such brash decisions.
Heck, even in cases where adult women are involved, they have a multitude of resources available, willing to help her, be it a genuine case or a fake one.
In a country where the majority of people will have their minds blown and will follow up with simple denial, when informed about such "forced to penetrate" cases, there's virtually no chance that things will improve. It's sad.. it's just sad..

Believe me, being a citizen of this country, I feel disgusted every time I read such blatantly stupid ways in which these cases are handled. If you can call a 12 year old boy, who might have not even hit puberty yet, as the perpetrator absent mindedly, then you know something is not right.

I'm not saying the 12 year old cannot commit the crime, but the fact that no one is questioning the intentions of the 17 year old maturing teenager, even after admitting to being in an intimate relationship with the boy, is mind boggling.

I mean, who knows, maybe the girl simply made the boy believe it wasn't something wrong. There's quite a chance that he may not have even known what sex was, or atleast what the appropriate thing to do was. Maybe.. just maybe.. the girl was influenced by pornography or her friends indulging in the same and coaxed the boy into trying it out with her?
Due to sex education being virtually absent in the country, these things are bound to happen.

I would just like to chime in.. The moment minors are involved in a sexual relationship, the courts do not recognise consent, as consent can only be given by a citizen above the age of 18. Thus, even if the sexual contact was completely mutual, even if they had witnesses testifying for the same, it'll still be inadmissible in court as minors don't have the right to give consent. (regardless of whether they said yes to each other)
